## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Wéimó jīng lüè shū* (T1778) is a ten-fascicle line-by-line exegetical commentary on Kumārajīva's translation of the *Vimalakīrti* ([KR6i0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0076) = T475). It is the verse-by-verse counterpart to the *Wéimó jīng xuán shū* ([KR6i0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0080) = T1777). Originally based on [智顗](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E9%A1%97) Zhīyǐ's lecture-records (lectures delivered at Yùquán sì 玉泉寺 in 593 CE in 28 fascicles, surviving as the *Wéimó jīng wén shū* 維摩經文疏 [KR6i0099](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0099) = X0338), the present *lüè shū* is the abridged 10-fascicle digest produced by the sixth Tiantai patriarch [湛然](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B9%9B%E7%84%B6) Zhànrán (711–782 CE) in the mid- to late-eighth century. The Taishō header cross-references No. 475 (the sūtra), 1777 (the *xuán shū*), and 1779 ([智圓](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E5%9C%93) Zhìyuán's *Chuíyù jì* sub-commentary).

**Abstract**

This text represents the consolidation of Tiantai *Vimalakīrti* exegesis into a usable scholastic format. Zhànrán was the sixth Tiantai patriarch (in the standard reckoning) and the chief restorer of the Tiantai tradition after the post-Huichang persecution period. His work consisted largely of commentaries on Zhīyǐ's *yízào* 遺造 (literary remains) — the *Făhuá xuányì shìqiān* 法華玄義釋籤 (T1717), the *Făhuá wén jù jì* 法華文句記 (T1719), and others — and his selective abridgment of Zhīyǐ's *Vimalakīrti* lecture-record into the present form.

The *Lüè shū* preserves Zhīyǐ's chapter-by-chapter exegesis of the *Vimalakīrti*, organized by the standard Tiantai hermeneutic apparatus. It is one of the two canonical Tiantai *Vimalakīrti* commentaries (with [KR6i0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0080)) and the basis for all subsequent Tiantai *Vimalakīrti* studies. Zhànrán's compositional dates are 711–782 CE; the *Lüè shū* is bracketed by his mature productivity period of 765–782 CE.
